description: A finger-picking trigger sequencer: each incoming pick moves through an eight-step pattern and fires one of six string triggers, with a matching note voltage.

params.text: Chooses the pattern, 1 to 50; the last two are the custom slots a Pick6p expander edits.
Chooses what happens at the end of a pattern: loop it, play the next pattern once and come back, or play a silent bar and come back.
Adds and removes notes as the pattern repeats: it moves picks off strings the chord mutes, drops picks from full patterns every eighth measure, and fills in skipped steps.

inputs.text: A rising edge past 2V moves the pattern on one step and fires the trigger for whichever string that step names.
A rising edge past 2V puts the sequence back before its first step and restarts the measure count.
Takes over the pattern knob while a cable is here: 0V to 10V spans the 50 patterns, and the knob is moved to follow.
Six channels of note voltage plus six channels of mute flag, where 0V plays the string and anything above 4.9V mutes it; a thirteenth channel is ignored.

outputs.text: The note voltage of the string the current step picked.
Six channels of trigger, one per string; a 10V pulse 1ms long comes out of the channel for the string that was picked.
A 10V pulse 1ms long on every step that picks a string, whichever string it was.

notes: Nothing moves until triggers arrive at PICK. The module has no clock of its own.
With nothing patched to POLY IN the six note voltages are those of an open E chord, so the CV output is useful with no chord source at all.
A Pick6p placed immediately to the right edits the last two patterns; a lamp in each module's name lights when they are joined.
menu: Muted Note CV to 0V — sends 0V out of the CV output on a step that is muted or skipped, instead of holding the previous step's voltage.
Smart Riff in Blank Pattern — lets the smart riff add notes while a blank pattern is playing, which is otherwise left silent.
Offset End Of Pattern — reverses the order of the end-of-pattern setting, so the next or silent bar is played first and the chosen pattern second.
